Fully local push-to-talk dictation for macOS.
Hold a key, speak, release: clean, correctly-spelled text appears at your cursor a second later.

> *you say:* "um so basically we should uh fine tune the model with pie torch, no wait, with MLX" > > *Flowstate types:* `So basically we should fine-tune the model with MLX.` ## Vision **Human-Machine Interaction.** I want the tool to disappear. For decades we shaped ourselves to the machine, learning to think in its keyboards, its syntax, its menus. I built Flowstate on the reverse bet: the machine should bend to us. Speech is our oldest interface, and I want the gap between a thought and its text to shrink to whatever the hardware allows. That closeness has to stay yours. Since the tool hears everything I say, I keep the whole loop on my own machine: my voice, my corrections, and my vocabulary never leave it, and it learns my words instead of demanding I learn its commands. I want an assistant quiet enough to vanish into the work, so that intention goes in and language comes out with nothing in between. ## Why this is different Dictation tools either send your voice to the cloud, or run locally and hand you raw, filler-riddled transcripts that mangle every technical term. Flowstate refuses both trade-offs: - **Nothing leaves your Mac.** Speech-to-text (whisper.cpp, Parakeet, Qwen3-ASR or Kyutai) and the cleanup LLM (llama.cpp, 3B) run as warm local child processes on loopback. No account, no API key, no subscription, works in airplane mode. Cloud (Groq) exists only as an explicit opt-in. - **It knows technical vocabulary out of the box.** ~610 built-in terms across software engineering, AI/ML, data science, econometrics, and quant finance (`PyTorch`, `kubectl`, `gRPC`, `Black-Scholes`, `heteroskedasticity`, `NeurIPS`, `Claude Code`, `Kimi`), biased into the recognizer per app context (code terms in editors, econ/AI terms everywhere). - **Three repair layers, engineered to never make things worse.** 1. *Decoder biasing*: your vocabulary is fed into Whisper's prompt (Qwen3-ASR reads it as context; Parakeet takes no prompt). 2. *Deterministic corrector*: a pure, exact-match pass fixes casing, hyphenation, and ~30 curated mishearings ("pie torch" → `PyTorch`, "cube control" → `kubectl`, "cloud code" → `Claude Code`) instantly, with structural guards so it can never rewrite ordinary English. 3. *Local LLM cleanup*: removes fillers, applies self-corrections ("meet at 2, no wait, 3" → "meet at 3"), repairs remaining misheard terms. ~0.3 s warm; a cold model falls back to the raw transcript rather than ever blocking your paste. A word-level guard then keeps only those edits: a paraphrase, a dropped clause, or an answer to a dictated question is reverted to your own words, so your sentences come through as you said them. - **It learns from you.** Fix a term in text Flowstate just pasted, and it notices (one Accessibility read-back of that same field). A correction that recurs joins your vocabulary automatically. Only the learned *term* is ever stored, never your document text. Fully local, capped, and one config flag to disable. - **Boring, auditable engineering.** Pure Swift/SwiftPM, zero external Swift dependencies, builds with Command Line Tools only (no Xcode). One binary, local child servers for speech and cleanup, 1068 tests including live integration against the real STT and LLM servers. ## Setup Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 13+, [Homebrew](https://brew.sh), and Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`). ### 1. Get the code and the speech model ```sh git clone https://github.com/henryph24/flowstate.git && cd flowstate brew install whisper-cpp MODELS="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Murmur/models" mkdir -p "$MODELS" # --fail: don't save an error page as the .bin; .partial + mv: an interrupted # download never looks installed. curl -L --fail --retry 3 -C - -o "$MODELS/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin.partial" \ "https://huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/resolve/main/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin" \ && mv "$MODELS/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin.partial" "$MODELS/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin" ``` (~1.6 GB, best accuracy. Lighter option: `ggml-small.en.bin`, ~490 MB, ~0.2 s per utterance; point `whisperModelPath` at it in the config.) ### 2. Install the local cleanup LLM (recommended) ```sh ./scripts/install_llama.sh ``` Installs llama.cpp via Homebrew and downloads a 3B instruct model (~2 GB). Skippable: dictation and the deterministic corrector work without it; you lose filler removal and phonetic repair. ### 3. Build and install the app ```sh ./scripts/make_app.sh open ~/Applications/Flowstate.app ``` ### 4. Permissions and the hotkey - **Microphone**: prompted on first recording. - **Accessibility**: prompted at launch (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility). Powers the global hotkey, the paste, and the optional auto-learn read-back (one read of the field you just dictated into; `"autoLearnEnabled": false` disables it). Accessibility is macOS's broadest permission: grant it only to software you trust; the source is here to audit. - **`fn` key**: System Settings → Keyboard → *"Press 🌐 key to"* → **Do Nothing**. Prefer another key? `"hotkey": "rightCommand"` in `~/.config/murmur/config.json`. Hold `fn`, say something, release. You're dictating. ### 5. (Recommended) A stable signing certificate macOS ties permission grants to the app's code signature; ad-hoc signatures change on every rebuild and silently kill the Accessibility grant. Once: Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → *Create a Certificate…* → name **Murmur Dev**, Identity Type *Self-Signed Root*, Certificate Type *Code Signing*. `make_app.sh` finds and uses it automatically. Recovery after a lost grant: `tccutil reset Accessibility dev.hungpq.murmur`, re-grant. ### Optional extras | What | How | |---|---| | Streaming STT (live words in the HUD) | `./scripts/install_kyutai.sh`, then menu → engine → Kyutai | | Fastest local STT (Parakeet TDT 0.6B) | `./scripts/install_parakeet.sh`, then menu → engine → Local Parakeet | | Faster STT that reads your vocabulary (Qwen3-ASR) | `./scripts/install_qwen_asr.sh`, then menu → engine → Local Qwen3-ASR | | Cloud STT/cleanup (Groq) | menu → *Set API Key…*; `"cleanupEngine": "groq"` for cloud cleanup | | Reuse a GGUF you already have | point `llamaModelPath` at any instruct GGUF (e.g. LM Studio's cache) | ### Choosing a speech engine Measured on an M3 Pro with warm servers: word error rate and median latency on 73 LibriSpeech recordings (real speech), and technical terms spelled right in the final text (after the corrector and cleanup) on 80 synthetic clips holding 16 terms such as `kubectl` and `scikit-learn`. | Engine (model) | Error rate | Latency | Terms right | Disk | |---|---|---|---|---| | whisper.cpp (large-v3-turbo), default | 5.4% | 0.72 s | 65/80 | 1.6 GB | | Parakeet (TDT 0.6B v2) | 2.9% | 0.09 s | 51/80 | 0.9 GB | | Parakeet (TDT 1.1B, `PARAKEET_MODEL=tdt-1.1b-q8_0.gguf`) | 1.9% | 0.10 s | 52/80 | 1.6 GB | | Parakeet (TDT 0.6B v3, 25 languages, `PARAKEET_MODEL=tdt-0.6b-v3-q8_0.gguf`) | 3.8% | 0.08 s | 57/80 | 0.9 GB | | Qwen3-ASR (0.6B) | 4.3% | 0.27 s | 66/80 | 1.0 GB | | Qwen3-ASR (1.7B, `QWEN_ASR_SIZE=1.7B`) | 4.1% | 0.69 s | 71/80 | 2.5 GB | The variables in the first column pick that model at install time; then set the config paths the script prints. Whisper was the most robust on an unusual synthetic voice (5% errors, Qwen3-ASR 8-13%, Parakeet 36-49%). Parakeet and Qwen3-ASR transcribe recordings longer than 60 s in 60 s pieces cut at pauses: a 10-minute recording takes 7.9 s on Parakeet, 18 s on Qwen3-ASR 0.6B and 29 s on Whisper. > **Groq is the one path that leaves your Mac.** Enabling it uploads your > recorded audio and the transcript (including any auto-learned vocabulary > terms) to Groq's API over HTTPS. Everything else (STT, cleanup, corrector, > auto-learn) is local. Your Groq API key is stored in cleartext at > `~/.config/murmur/config.json` (file mode `0600`, in a `0700` directory). ## Using it - **Hold to talk**; a pill HUD shows state. Release to transcribe and paste into the frontmost app. Tap any other key while holding (or release within 0.25 s) to cancel. - **Password fields**: in secure-input contexts Flowstate never types; the text is placed on the clipboard for you to paste, marked *concealed*, and cleared ~60 s later (restoring your previous clipboard) unless you replace it first. - **Clipboard-safe**: your previous clipboard is snapshotted and restored ~0.6 s after the paste (unless you copied something new meanwhile). Dictated text is marked *concealed* / auto-generated, so clipboard managers and Universal Clipboard skip it instead of archiving every utterance. - **Menu bar**: engine picker, AI Cleanup toggle, Dock icon, start at login. ## Vocabulary: built-in, yours, and learned Built-in terms are always on (`"builtinVocabularyEnabled": false` opts out). Your own terms in `~/.config/murmur/config.json` win over built-ins (budget, casing, everything): ```jsonc { "customVocabulary": ["Jane Doe", "VNDirect", "quintile portfolio"], // every app "codeVocabulary": ["MurmurKit", "FnStateMachine"], // editors/terminals only "vocabularyAliases": { "vee end direct": "VNDirect" } // spoken-form fixes } ``` Auto-learn adds terms you correct by hand (≥2 recurrences, 50-term cap, oldest evicted; sidecar `~/.config/murmur/autolearn.json` stores terms only). `"autoLearnEnabled": false` disables it. ## Configuration reference `~/.config/murmur/config.json`: every key optional; defaults shown. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""STT benchmark for whisper-server configs (good-night session scratch tool).

Synthesizes fixture utterances with macOS `say` (several accents), then runs each
whisper-server configuration on a private loopback port and reports warm latency
and WER. TTS speech is cleaner than real speech: trust the latency deltas fully,
treat WER deltas as a smoke signal.

usage: stt_bench.py <config-name> [<config-name> ...]   (see CONFIGS)
"""
import json, os, re, subprocess, sys, time, urllib.request, uuid

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
FIX = os.path.join(HERE, "stt_fixtures")
MODELS = os.path.expanduser("~/Library/Application Support/Murmur/models")
PORT = 18923
BIN = "/opt/homebrew/bin/whisper-server"
THREADS = str(max(4, os.cpu_count() // 2))

SENTENCES = [
    "We should fine-tune the model with PyTorch and then export it to ONNX.",
    "Run kubectl get pods to see which containers are failing in the staging cluster.",
    "The regression shows heteroskedasticity, so we need robust standard errors.",
    "I think we should push the release to Thursday because the migration isn't ready yet.",
    "Can you take a look at the pull request when you get a chance? I left a few comments on the error handling.",
    "Let's store the embeddings in PostgreSQL and cache the hot keys in Redis.",
    "The Black-Scholes model assumes constant volatility, which is obviously not true in practice.",
    "Open the project in Xcode and run the SwiftPM build before you push to main.",
    "Yesterday I spent most of the afternoon debugging the deployment, and it turned out the environment variable for the database URL was pointing at the staging cluster instead of production.",
    "We use LangChain for retrieval and scikit-learn for the baseline classifier.",
    "The model was trained with RLHF and then distilled into a smaller student.",
    "Please install NumPy and pandas, then rerun the notebook from the top.",
    "Honestly I don't love this approach, but it's probably the fastest way to unblock the team.",
    "If the Sharpe ratio holds up out of sample, we should present it at the next research meeting.",
    "The gRPC service times out whenever the payload is larger than four megabytes.",
    "Send the quarterly report to Alice and copy the finance team on the thread.",
]
VOCAB_TERMS = ["PyTorch", "ONNX", "kubectl", "heteroskedasticity", "PostgreSQL", "Redis",
               "Black-Scholes", "Xcode", "SwiftPM", "LangChain", "scikit-learn", "RLHF",
               "NumPy", "pandas", "Sharpe ratio", "gRPC"]
VOICES = ["Samantha", "Daniel", "Karen", "Moira", "Rishi"]

BENCH_MODELS = os.path.join(HERE, "models")
PARAKEET_BIN = os.environ.get("PARAKEET_BIN", os.path.join(
    "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hungpq2412-flowstate/d9f69700-55f7-49d1-9658-95e55f0075c7/scratchpad",
    "parakeet-bin/parakeet-v0.5.0-bin-macos-metal-arm64/parakeet-server"))
LLAMA_BIN = "/opt/homebrew/bin/llama-server"

def m(name):
    return os.path.join(MODELS, name)

def b(name):
    return os.path.join(BENCH_MODELS, name)

BASE = ["-l", "en", "-sns", "--carry-initial-prompt", "-t", THREADS]
ENGINES = {}  # name -> (kind, model, extra); kind in whisper|parakeet|qwen
CONFIGS = {
    "turbo-bs5":        (m("ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "5", "-bo", "5"]),
    "turbo-greedy":     (m("ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "-1", "-bo", "1"]),
    "turbo-bs2":        (m("ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "2", "-bo", "2"]),
    "turbo-q5-bs5":     (m("ggml-large-v3-turbo-q5_0.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "5", "-bo", "5"]),
    "turbo-q5-greedy":  (m("ggml-large-v3-turbo-q5_0.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "-1", "-bo", "1"]),
    "turbo-q8-bs5":     (m("ggml-large-v3-turbo-q8_0.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "5", "-bo", "5"]),
    "turbo-q8-greedy":  (m("ggml-large-v3-turbo-q8_0.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "-1", "-bo", "1"]),
    "small.en-bs5":     (m("ggml-small.en.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "5", "-bo", "5"]),
    "distil35-bs5":     (b("ggml-distil-large-v3.5.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "5", "-bo", "5"]),
    "distil35-greedy":  (b("ggml-distil-large-v3.5.bin"), BASE + ["-bs", "-1", "-bo", "1"]),
}
for _n, (_mod, _x) in CONFIGS.items():
    ENGINES[_n] = ("whisper", _mod, _x)
for _v in ["tdt-0.6b-v2-q8_0", "tdt-0.6b-v2-f16", "tdt-0.6b-v3-q8_0", "tdt-1.1b-q8_0", "tdt_ctc-1.1b-q8_0"]:
    ENGINES["pk-" + _v] = ("parakeet", b(_v + ".gguf"), ["--threads", THREADS])
for _q in ["0.6B", "1.7B"]:
    ENGINES["qwen-" + _q] = ("qwen", b(f"Qwen3-ASR-{_q}-Q8_0.gguf"),
                            ["--mmproj", b(f"mmproj-Qwen3-ASR-{_q}-Q8_0.gguf"),
                             "-c", "4096", "-ngl", "99", "-t", THREADS])

def norm_words(s):
    s = s.lower().replace("’", "'").replace("-", " ")
    return [w for w in re.split(r"[^a-z0-9']+", s) if w.strip("'")]

def edit_distance(a, b):
    prev = list(range(len(b) + 1))
    for i in range(1, len(a) + 1):
        cur = [i] + [0] * len(b)
        for j in range(1, len(b) + 1):
            cur[j] = min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j - 1] + 1, prev[j - 1] + (a[i - 1] != b[j - 1]))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]

def build_fixtures():
    os.makedirs(FIX, exist_ok=True)
    items = []
    for vi, voice in enumerate(VOICES):
        for si, text in enumerate(SENTENCES):
            wav = os.path.join(FIX, f"{voice}-{si:02d}.wav")
            if not os.path.exists(wav):
                aiff = wav[:-4] + ".aiff"
                subprocess.run(["say", "-v", voice, "-o", aiff, text], check=True)
                # 0.25 s lead-in / 0.15 s tail, like a push-to-talk capture
                subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-i", aiff,
                                "-af", "adelay=250,apad=pad_dur=0.15,loudnorm=I=-20",
                                "-ar", "16000", "-ac", "1", "-sample_fmt", "s16", wav], check=True)
                os.remove(aiff)
            items.append((voice, si, text, wav))
    return items

def multipart(fields, wav_bytes):
    boundary = uuid.uuid4().hex
    body = b""
    for k, v in fields.items():
        body += f"--{boundary}\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"\r\n\r\n{v}\r\n".encode()
    body += (f"--{boundary}\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"file\"; filename=\"a.wav\"\r\n"
             f"Content-Type: audio/wav\r\n\r\n").encode() + wav_bytes + f"\r\n--{boundary}--\r\n".encode()
    return boundary, body

AUDIO_CTX = os.environ.get("AUDIO_CTX")  # "auto" -> per-request ctx from clip duration

KIND = "whisper"

def transcribe(wav_path, prompt):
    if KIND == "parakeet":
        boundary, body = multipart({"response_format": "json"}, open(wav_path, "rb").read())
        req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/v1/audio/transcriptions", data=body,
                                     method="POST",
                                     headers={"Content-Type": f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}"})
        t0 = time.time()
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
            text = json.loads(r.read())["text"].strip()
        return text, time.time() - t0
    if KIND == "qwen":
        import base64
        content = [{"type": "input_audio",
                    "input_audio": {"data": base64.b64encode(open(wav_path, "rb").read()).decode(),
                                    "format": "wav"}}]
        messages = []
        if QWEN_CONTEXT and prompt:
            messages.append({"role": "system", "content": prompt})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": content})
        if QWEN_PREFILL:
            messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": "language English<asr_text>"})
        body = json.dumps({"messages": messages, "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 2048,
                           "cache_prompt": False}).encode()
        req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/v1/chat/completions", data=body,
                                     method="POST", headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        t0 = time.time()
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
            raw = json.loads(r.read())["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or ""
        dt = time.time() - t0
        text = raw.split("<asr_text>", 1)[1] if "<asr_text>" in raw else raw
        return text.strip(), dt
    return transcribe_whisper(wav_path, prompt)

QWEN_CONTEXT = os.environ.get("QWEN_CONTEXT") == "1"
QWEN_PREFILL = os.environ.get("QWEN_PREFILL") == "1"

def transcribe_whisper(wav_path, prompt):
    fields = {"temperature": "0", "response_format": "json"}
    if AUDIO_CTX:
        dur = (os.path.getsize(wav_path) - 44) / 32000.0
        fields["audio_ctx"] = str(min(1500, int((dur + float(os.environ.get("CTX_PAD", "1.0"))) * 50) + 1)) if AUDIO_CTX == "auto" else AUDIO_CTX
    if prompt:
        fields["prompt"] = prompt
    boundary, body = multipart(fields, open(wav_path, "rb").read())
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/inference", data=body, method="POST",
                                 headers={"Content-Type": f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}"})
    t0 = time.time()
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
        text = json.loads(r.read())["text"].strip()
    return text, time.time() - t0

def wait_ready(proc):
    path = "/" if KIND == "whisper" else "/health"
    for _ in range(480):
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            raise RuntimeError("server exited")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}{path}", timeout=1) as r:
                if r.status == 200:
                    return
        except Exception:
            pass
        time.sleep(0.25)
    raise RuntimeError("server not ready")

def main():
    names = sys.argv[1:] or ["turbo-bs5"]
    prompt = "" if os.environ.get("NOPROMPT") else subprocess.run([os.path.join(HERE, ".build/debug/Bench"), "--whisper-prompt", "code"],
                            capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    if os.environ.get("LONG"):
        refs = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, "long_fixtures", os.environ.get("LONG_REFS", "refs.json"))))
        items = [("long", i, r["text"], os.path.join(HERE, r["wav"])) for i, r in enumerate(refs)]
    elif os.environ.get("REAL"):
        refs = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, "real_fixtures", "refs.json")))
        items = [("ls", i, r["text"], os.path.join(HERE, r["wav"])) for i, r in enumerate(refs)]
    else:
        items = build_fixtures()
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(HERE, "results"), exist_ok=True)
    global KIND
    for name in names:
        KIND, model, extra = ENGINES[name]
        if not os.path.exists(model):
            print(f"{name}: model missing ({model})"); continue
        if KIND == "whisper":
            cmd = [BIN, "-m", model, "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(PORT)] + extra
        elif KIND == "parakeet":
            cmd = [PARAKEET_BIN, "--model", model, "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(PORT)] + extra
        else:
            cmd = [LLAMA_BIN, "-m", model, "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(PORT)] + extra
        log = open(os.path.join(HERE, "results", f"server-{name}.log"), "w")
        rss_peak = 0
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=log, stderr=log)
        try:
            wait_ready(proc)
            transcribe(items[0][3], prompt)  # warm
            rows, errs, words, lat, hits, total_terms = [], 0, 0, [], 0, 0
            for voice, si, text, wav in items:
                hyp, dt = transcribe(wav, prompt)
                ref_w, hyp_w = norm_words(text), norm_words(hyp)
                e = edit_distance(ref_w, hyp_w)
                errs += e; words += len(ref_w); lat.append(dt)
                for term in VOCAB_TERMS:
                    if term.lower() in text.lower():
                        total_terms += 1
                        hits += term.lower() in hyp.lower()
                rows.append({"voice": voice, "i": si, "ref": text, "hyp": hyp, "errors": e, "latency": dt})
            lat.sort()
            p50, p90 = lat[len(lat) // 2], lat[int(len(lat) * 0.9)]
            print(f"{name + os.environ.get('TAG', ''):16s} WER {errs / words:.3%} ({errs}/{words})  exact-terms {hits}/{total_terms}  "
                  f"p50 {p50:.2f}s  p90 {p90:.2f}s  mean {sum(lat) / len(lat):.2f}s  n={len(lat)}")
            tag = ("long-" if os.environ.get("LONG") else "real-" if os.environ.get("REAL") else "") \
                + os.environ.get("TAG", "")
            try:
                rss = subprocess.run(["ps", "-o", "rss=", "-p", str(proc.pid)], capture_output=True,
                                     text=True).stdout.strip()
                print(f"{'':16s} server RSS {int(rss) / 1024:.0f} MB")
            except Exception:
                pass
            json.dump(rows, open(os.path.join(HERE, "results", f"stt-{tag.split('-')[0] + '-' if tag.startswith(('real', 'long')) else ''}{name}{os.environ.get('TAG', '')}.json"), "w"), indent=1)
        finally:
            proc.terminate(); proc.wait()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Times the app's exact requests against the running Flowstate servers."""
import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request

S = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
P = json.load(open(os.path.join(S, "prompts.json")))
QWEN = int(os.environ.get("QWEN_PORT", "8727"))
LLAMA = int(os.environ.get("LLAMA_PORT", "8725"))

def post(port, body, timeout=120):
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/chat/completions",
                                 data=json.dumps(body).encode(), method="POST",
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
        out = json.loads(r.read())
    return out, time.time() - t0

def health(port):
    t0 = time.time()
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health", timeout=5) as r:
        r.read()
    return time.time() - t0

def qwen(wav_path, ctx="whisper_general"):
    wav = open(wav_path, "rb").read()
    seconds = max(0, len(wav) - 44) / 32000
    body = {"messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": P[ctx]},
        {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {
            "data": base64.b64encode(wav).decode(), "format": "wav"}}]},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "language English<asr_text>"}],
        "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": int(seconds * 8) + 64, "cache_prompt": True}
    out, dt = post(QWEN, body)
    text = out["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or ""
    if "<asr_text>" in text:
        text = text.split("<asr_text>", 1)[1]
    text = text.split("</asr_text>", 1)[0].strip()
    return text, dt, out.get("timings", {}), seconds

def cleanup(text):
    words = len(text.split())
    body = {"messages": [{"role": "system", "content": P["cleanup_system"]},
                         {"role": "user", "content": f"<transcript>\n{text}\n</transcript>"}],
            "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": max(80, words * 2 + 60), "cache_prompt": True}
    out, dt = post(LLAMA, body)
    return out["choices"][0]["message"]["content"], dt, out.get("timings", {})

def fmt(t):
    return (f"prompt_n={t.get('prompt_n')} cache_n={t.get('cache_n')} prompt_ms={t.get('prompt_ms', 0):.0f} "
            f"gen_n={t.get('predicted_n')} gen_ms={t.get('predicted_ms', 0):.0f}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    wavs = sys.argv[1:]
    rounds = int(os.environ.get("ROUNDS", "1"))
    for r in range(rounds):
        for w in wavs:
            h1 = health(QWEN)
            text, dq, tq, sec = qwen(w)
            h2 = health(LLAMA)
            cleaned, dc, tc = cleanup(text)
            print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {os.path.basename(w)} {sec:.1f}s audio | "
                  f"health {h1*1000:.0f}/{h2*1000:.0f} ms | STT {dq:.2f}s ({fmt(tq)}) | "
                  f"cleanup {dc:.2f}s ({fmt(tc)}) | total {dq+dc:.2f}s", flush=True)
EOF

S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hungpq2412-flowstate/8432bfbd-ac76-4330-b4e2-211cab79f7b4/scratchpad
cat > "$S/idle_probe.py" <<'EOF'
"""Spawns the app's two servers (exact app arguments), lets them sit idle, and
times the first pipeline request after each idle period, with the servers'
swapped and resident memory sampled before it."""
import base64, json, os, re, subprocess, sys, time, urllib.request

S = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
P = json.load(open(os.path.join(S, "prompts.json")))
M = os.path.expanduser("~/Library/Application Support/Murmur/models")
BIN = "/opt/homebrew/bin/llama-server"
TAG = os.environ.get("TAG", "base")
EXTRA = os.environ.get("EXTRA", "").split()
IDLES = [float(x) for x in os.environ.get("IDLES", "2,5,10,15").split(",")]
WAV = sys.argv[1]
CPORT, QPORT = int(os.environ.get("CPORT", "18845")), int(os.environ.get("QPORT", "18947"))

def spawn(args, name):
    log = open(os.path.join(S, f"idle-{TAG}-{name}.log"), "w")
    return subprocess.Popen([BIN] + args + EXTRA, stdout=log, stderr=log)

cleanup = spawn(["-m", f"{M}/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(CPORT),
                 "-c", "4096", "-ngl", "99", "-t", "6"], "cleanup")
qwen = spawn(["-m", f"{M}/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-Q8_0.gguf", "--mmproj", f"{M}/mmproj-Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-Q8_0.gguf",
              "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(QPORT), "-c", "4096", "-ngl", "99", "-t", "6"], "qwen")

def ready(port):
    for _ in range(480):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health", timeout=1) as r:
                if r.status == 200:
                    return
        except Exception:
            pass
        time.sleep(0.25)
    raise SystemExit(f"port {port} not ready")

def post(port, body):
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 method="POST", headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:
        out = json.loads(r.read())
    return out, time.time() - t0

wav = open(WAV, "rb").read()
secs = (len(wav) - 44) / 32000

def pipeline():
    q, dq = post(QPORT, {"messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": P["whisper_general"]},
        {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": base64.b64encode(wav).decode(), "format": "wav"}}]},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "language English<asr_text>"}],
        "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": int(secs * 8) + 64, "cache_prompt": True})
    text = (q["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or "").split("<asr_text>")[-1].split("</asr_text>")[0].strip()
    c, dc = post(CPORT, {"messages": [{"role": "system", "content": P["cleanup_system"]},
                                     {"role": "user", "content": f"<transcript>\n{text}\n</transcript>"}],
                         "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": max(80, len(text.split()) * 2 + 60), "cache_prompt": True})
    tq, tc = q.get("timings", {}), c.get("timings", {})
    return {"stt": round(dq, 3), "stt_server_ms": round(tq.get("prompt_ms", 0) + tq.get("predicted_ms", 0)),
            "stt_prompt_n": tq.get("prompt_n"), "cleanup": round(dc, 3),
            "cleanup_server_ms": round(tc.get("prompt_ms", 0) + tc.get("predicted_ms", 0)),
            "cleanup_prompt_n": tc.get("prompt_n"), "words": len(text.split())}

def mem(pid):
    out = subprocess.run(["vmmap", "-summary", str(pid)], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    w = re.search(r"Writable regions: Total=(\S+) written=(\S+) resident=(\S+) swapped_out=(\S+)", out)
    mf = next((l.split() for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith("mapped file")), None)
    fp = re.search(r"Physical footprint:\s+(\S+)", out)
    return {"swapped": w.group(4) if w else None, "anon_resident": w.group(3) if w else None,
            "file_resident": mf[3] if mf else None, "footprint": fp.group(1) if fp else None}

def snap():
    swap = subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "vm.swapusage"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    return {"cleanup": mem(cleanup.pid), "qwen": mem(qwen.pid), "swap": swap.split("used = ")[1].split()[0]}

def emit(row):
    row["t"] = time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")
    print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)

try:
    ready(CPORT); ready(QPORT)
    for _ in range(2):
        emit({"phase": "warm", **pipeline()})
    for idle in IDLES:
        end = time.time() + idle * 60
        while time.time() < end:
            time.sleep(min(60, max(0, end - time.time())))
            emit({"phase": "idle", "idle_min": idle, "mem": snap()})
        emit({"phase": "after_idle", "idle_min": idle, **pipeline()})
        emit({"phase": "warm_again", "idle_min": idle, **pipeline()})
finally:
    cleanup.terminate(); qwen.terminate()
    cleanup.wait(); qwen.wait()
EOF

import PackageDescription

let package = Package(
    name: "Murmur",
    platforms: [.macOS(.v13)],
    targets: [
        .target(name: "MurmurKit"),

#!/bin/bash
# Builds Flowstate.app from the SwiftPM release binary and installs it to
# ~/Applications. Signs with the stable "Murmur Dev" self-signed identity when
# present (keeps TCC grants alive across rebuilds), else falls back to ad-hoc.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

swift build -c release

APP=build/Flowstate.app
rm -rf "$APP"
mkdir -p "$APP/Contents/MacOS" "$APP/Contents/Resources"
cp Resources/Info.plist "$APP/Contents/Info.plist"
cp Resources/murmur.icns "$APP/Contents/Resources/murmur.icns"
cp .build/release/Murmur "$APP/Contents/MacOS/Flowstate"
printf 'APPL????' > "$APP/Contents/PkgInfo"

# A self-signed cert won't appear under the codesigning *policy* filter, but
# codesign can still sign with it by name — check the cert exists instead.
if security find-certificate -c "Murmur Dev" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    IDENTITY="Murmur Dev"
else
    IDENTITY="-"
    cat >&2 <<'EOF'
WARNING: no "Murmur Dev" certificate found — signing ad-hoc.
         Accessibility/Microphone grants will NOT survive rebuilds.
         One-time fix: Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → Create a
         Certificate… → Name: "Murmur Dev", Identity Type: Self-Signed Root,
         Certificate Type: Code Signing → Create. Then rerun this script.
EOF
fi

# --options runtime: hardened runtime, so another same-user process can't
# DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES or debugger-attach into an app holding Accessibility +
# Microphone. Self-signed "Murmur Dev" still satisfies TCC persistence. (Add
# --timestamp for a notarizable build; it needs network, so it's left off here.)
codesign --force --options runtime --sign "$IDENTITY" "$APP"
codesign --verify --strict "$APP"

mkdir -p ~/Applications
rm -rf ~/Applications/Murmur.app ~/Applications/Flowstate.app
ditto "$APP" ~/Applications/Flowstate.app

echo "Signed with: $IDENTITY"
echo "Installed:   ~/Applications/Flowstate.app  (launch with: open ~/Applications/Flowstate.app)"
public final class ParakeetEngine: TranscriptionEngine, LocalServerEngine {
    /// Attention cost grows with the square of the length: on an M3 Pro a
    /// 600 s recording takes 43 s and 3.3 GB in one pass, 7.9 s in 60 s chunks.
    public static let maxChunkSeconds = 60.0

    private let binaryPath: String
    private let modelPath: String
    private let session: URLSession
    private let server: ChildServer

    public init(binaryPath: String, modelPath: String, port: Int,
                session: URLSession = LoopbackURLSession.make(resourceTimeout: 90)) {
        let binary = (binaryPath as NSString).expandingTildeInPath
        let model = (modelPath as NSString).expandingTildeInPath
        self.binaryPath = binary
        self.modelPath = model
        self.session = session
        self.server = ChildServer(name: "parakeet-server", binaryPath: binary, port: port,
                                  session: session) { port in
            Self.serverArguments(modelPath: model, port: port)
        }
    }

    deinit { shutdown() }

    /// `prompt` is ignored: Parakeet has no decoder prompt.
    public func transcribe(wav: Data, prompt: String?) async throws -> String {
        try await ensureServerRunning()
        return try await AudioChunker.transcribe(wav: wav, maxSeconds: Self.maxChunkSeconds) { piece in
            try await ensureServerRunning() // a retry after a crash respawns the server
            let request = Self.makeTranscriptionRequest(wav: piece, port: server.port)
            let (data, response) = try await session.data(for: request)
            let status = (response as? HTTPURLResponse)?.statusCode ?? 0
            guard status == 200 else { throw ParakeetError.http(status: status) }
            return try Self.parseResponse(data)
        }
                                            prompt: String? = nil) -> URLRequest {
        var multipart = MultipartBody()
        multipart.addField(name: "temperature", value: "0")
        multipart.addField(name: "response_format", value: "json")
        if let prompt, !prompt.isEmpty {
            multipart.addField(name: "prompt", value: prompt)
        }
        multipart.addFile(name: "file", filename: "audio.wav", contentType: "audio/wav", data: wav)
        var request = URLRequest(url: URL(string: "http://127.0.0.1:\(port)/inference")!)
        request.httpMethod = "POST"
        request.setValue(multipart.contentType, forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
        request.httpBody = multipart.finalized()
        request.timeoutInterval = 60
        return request
    }
}

def post(port, body):

           + b"data" + (32000).to_bytes(4, "little") + bytes(32000))

def pipeline():
    wav = CLIPS[COUNTER[0] % len(CLIPS)]
    COUNTER[0] += 1
    secs = (len(wav) - 44) / 32000
    q, dq = post(QPORT, stt_body(wav, int(secs * 8) + 64))
    text = (q["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or "").split("<asr_text>")[-1].split("</asr_text>")[0].strip()
    c, dc = post(CPORT, cleanup_body(text, max(80, len(text.split()) * 2 + 60)))
    return {"stt": round(dq, 3), "cleanup": round(dc, 3), "total": round(dq + dc, 3),
            "stt_srv": round(q["timings"]["prompt_ms"] + q["timings"]["predicted_ms"]),
            "cleanup_srv": round(c["timings"]["prompt_ms"] + c["timings"]["predicted_ms"]),
            "stt_pn": q["timings"]["prompt_n"], "cleanup_pn": c["timings"]["prompt_n"], "audio_s": round(secs, 2)}

def prewarm():
    took = {}
    def stt():
        _, took["stt_warm"] = post(QPORT, stt_body(SILENCE, 1))
    def clean():
        _, took["cleanup_warm"] = post(CPORT, cleanup_body("ok", 1))
    threads = [threading.Thread(target=stt), threading.Thread(target=clean)]
    for t in threads:
        t.start()
    return threads, took

def evict():
    out = subprocess.run([os.path.join(S, "fcache"), "-e"] + FILES, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    return " | ".join(l.split(": ", 1)[1] for l in out.strip().splitlines())

def emit(row):
    row["t"] = time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")
    print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
  try:
    ready(CPORT); ready(QPORT)
    for _ in range(2):
        emit({"trial": "warmup", **pipeline()})
    for r in range(ROUNDS):
        cache = evict()
        emit({"trial": "evicted_plain", "round": r, "evict": cache, **pipeline()})
        emit({"trial": "warm", "round": r, **pipeline()})
        for hold in HOLDS:
            cache = evict()
            threads, took = prewarm()
            time.sleep(hold)
            row = pipeline()
            for t in threads:
                t.join()
            emit({"trial": f"evicted_prewarm_{hold:g}s", "round": r, "evict": cache, **took, **row})
            emit({"trial": "warm", "round": r, **pipeline()})
  finally:
    cleanup.terminate(); qwen.terminate()
    cleanup.wait(); qwen.wait()

Dictation tools either send your voice to the cloud, or run locally and hand

- **Nothing leaves your Mac.** Speech-to-text (whisper.cpp, Parakeet,
  Qwen3-ASR or Kyutai) and the cleanup LLM (llama.cpp, 3B) run as warm local
  child processes on loopback. No account, no API key, no subscription, works
  in airplane mode. Cloud (Groq) exists only as an explicit opt-in.

- **It knows technical vocabulary out of the box.** ~610 built-in terms across
  software engineering, AI/ML, data science, econometrics, and quant finance
  (`PyTorch`, `kubectl`, `gRPC`, `Black-Scholes`, `heteroskedasticity`,
  `NeurIPS`, `Claude Code`, `Kimi`), biased into the recognizer per app
  context (code terms in editors, econ/AI terms everywhere).

- **Three repair layers, engineered to never make things worse.**
  1. *Decoder biasing*: your vocabulary is fed into Whisper's prompt
     (Qwen3-ASR reads it as context; Parakeet takes no prompt).
  2. *Deterministic corrector*: a pure, exact-match pass fixes casing,
     hyphenation, and ~30 curated mishearings ("pie torch" → `PyTorch`,
     "cube control" → `kubectl`, "cloud code" → `Claude Code`) instantly,
     with structural guards so it can never rewrite ordinary English.
  3. *Local LLM cleanup*: removes fillers, applies self-corrections
     ("meet at 2, no wait, 3" → "meet at 3"), repairs remaining misheard
     terms. ~0.3 s warm; a cold model falls back to the raw transcript
     rather than ever blocking your paste. A word-level guard then keeps
     only those edits: a paraphrase, a dropped clause, or an answer to a
     dictated question is reverted to your own words, so your sentences
     come through as you said them.

- **It learns from you.** Fix a term in text Flowstate just pasted, and it
  notices (one Accessibility read-back of that same field). A correction that
  recurs joins your vocabulary automatically. Only the learned *term* is ever
  stored, never your document text. Fully local, capped, and one config flag
  to disable.

- **Boring, auditable engineering.** Pure Swift/SwiftPM, zero external Swift
  dependencies, builds with Command Line Tools only (no Xcode). One binary,
  local child servers for speech and cleanup, 1068 tests including live
  integration against the real STT and LLM servers.

#!/bin/bash
# Builds Flowstate.app from the SwiftPM release binary and installs it to
# ~/Applications. Signs with the stable "Murmur Dev" self-signed identity when
# present (keeps TCC grants alive across rebuilds), else falls back to ad-hoc.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

swift build -c release

APP=build/Flowstate.app
rm -rf "$APP"
mkdir -p "$APP/Contents/MacOS" "$APP/Contents/Resources"
cp Resources/Info.plist "$APP/Contents/Info.plist"
cp Resources/murmur.icns "$APP/Contents/Resources/murmur.icns"
cp .build/release/Murmur "$APP/Contents/MacOS/Flowstate"
printf 'APPL????' > "$APP/Contents/PkgInfo"

# A self-signed cert won't appear under the codesigning *policy* filter, but
# codesign can still sign with it by name — check the cert exists instead.
if security find-certificate -c "Murmur Dev" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    IDENTITY="Murmur Dev"
else
    IDENTITY="-"
    cat >&2 <<'EOF'
WARNING: no "Murmur Dev" certificate found — signing ad-hoc.
         Accessibility/Microphone grants will NOT survive rebuilds.
         One-time fix: Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → Create a
         Certificate… → Name: "Murmur Dev", Identity Type: Self-Signed Root,
         Certificate Type: Code Signing → Create. Then rerun this script.
EOF
fi

# --options runtime: hardened runtime, so another same-user process can't
# DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES or debugger-attach into an app holding Accessibility +
# Microphone. Self-signed "Murmur Dev" still satisfies TCC persistence. (Add
# --timestamp for a notarizable build; it needs network, so it's left off here.)
codesign --force --options runtime --sign "$IDENTITY" "$APP"
codesign --verify --strict "$APP"

mkdir -p ~/Applications
rm -rf ~/Applications/Murmur.app ~/Applications/Flowstate.app
ditto "$APP" ~/Applications/Flowstate.app

echo "Signed with: $IDENTITY"
echo "Installed:   ~/Applications/Flowstate.app  (launch with: open ~/Applications/Flowstate.app)"

import ctypes, ctypes.util, os, sys, time, struct, fcntl
libc = ctypes.CDLL(ctypes.util.find_library('c'), use_errno=True)
libc.mmap.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
libc.mmap.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_longlong]
libc.munmap.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t]
libc.mincore.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_char_p]
PAGE = os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE')
F_RDADVISE = 44

def resident_mb(path):
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
    size = os.fstat(fd).st_size
    addr = libc.mmap(None, size, 1, 1, fd, 0)  # PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED
    n = (size + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
    vec = ctypes.create_string_buffer(n)
    rc = libc.mincore(addr, size, vec)
    res = sum(1 for b in vec.raw[:n] if b & 1)
    libc.munmap(addr, size)
    os.close(fd)
    return rc, res * PAGE / 1e6, size / 1e6

mode = sys.argv[1]
path = sys.argv[2]
if mode == 'check':
    print(path, resident_mb(path))
    sys.exit(0)
# mode 'advise': same loop as Prewarm.readAhead (1 GiB chunks)
rc, r0, total = resident_mb(path)
print(f"before: resident {r0:.0f} of {total:.0f} MB")
fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
size = os.fstat(fd).st_size
chunk = 1 << 30
off = 0
t0 = time.monotonic()
while off < size:
    fcntl.fcntl(fd, F_RDADVISE, struct.pack('qi4x', off, min(chunk, size - off)))
    off += chunk
dt = time.monotonic() - t0
os.close(fd)
_, r1, _ = resident_mb(path)
print(f"fcntl loop returned after {dt*1000:.0f} ms; resident right after: {r1:.0f} MB")
for i in range(8):
    time.sleep(0.5)
    _, r, _ = resident_mb(path)
    print(f"  +{(i+1)*0.5:.1f} s: resident {r:.0f} MB")

"""Evicts a file that no running process maps, runs the app's read-ahead loop
(radvise: fcntl F_RDADVISE in 1 GiB chunks), then samples page-cache residency
right after it returns and every 0.5 s for 4 s."""
import os, subprocess, sys, time
S = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
def cached(path):
    out = subprocess.run([os.path.join(S, "fcache"), path], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    return out.strip().split("cached ")[-1]
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    subprocess.run([os.path.join(S, "fcache"), "-e", path], capture_output=True)
    before = cached(path)
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    subprocess.run([os.path.join(S, "radvise"), path], check=True)
    took = time.monotonic() - t0
    samples = [cached(path)]
    for _ in range(8):
        time.sleep(0.5)
        samples.append(cached(path))
    print(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: before {before}; returned in {took*1000:.0f} ms; after: {' > '.join(samples)}", flush=True)
EOF

def cached():

        rows[name].append((round(took, 2), now, later))

### Steps
- Stopped the first independent check: it had been waiting 40 minutes on an approval prompt. Its notes showed the read-ahead fell short under memory pressure.
- Confirmed that gap myself. Replaced the read-ahead with plain reads of only the parts not yet in memory, and wrote the test first.
- Measured the whole dictation path again, this time on the app's own servers.
- Reinstalled and restarted the app, updated the docs, and recorded the lessons in the new lesson files.
- Started a second independent check with a 20-minute limit and a rule against deleting files.

### Done
- Verified (`ra_ab.py`, 4 alternating rounds on a 1,549 MB file):
  - Old read-ahead: once left only 1,091 MB in memory right after it returned, and lost pages within 2 s in 3 of the 4 rounds.
  - New read-ahead: kept all 1,549 MB in memory, right after it returned and 2 s later, in all 4 rounds.
- Verified (`.build/debug/MurmurTests`): the new live test failed on the old code ("1113 passed, 4 failed", 76-77% of the file in memory). It passes on the new code ("1117 passed, 0 failed").
- Verified (`pressure_probe.py` on the app's own servers), for a 5 s dictation after memory pressure:
  - 0.88-1.09 s after a 3 s hold.
  - 1.08-1.83 s after a 1 s hold.
  - 5.78-6.19 s without the warm-up.
- Verified (`fcache`): after the app sat idle for 45 minutes, macOS had dropped 1,238 MB of its 1,926 MB cleanup model from memory. This is the live cause of the slowdown.
- Verified (`make_app.sh`, `codesign --verify --strict`, `nm`): the installed app is signed with "Murmur Dev" and contains the new read-ahead (it imports `pread` and `mincore`).
- Verified (health checks): the restarted app runs as pid 74811. Its servers 74843 (port 8725) and 74842 (port 8727) answered 200 after 5 checks.

### Not done
- The second independent check is running and has not reported yet.
- The Groq test is skipped, because there is no .env and no GROQ_API_KEY.
- I did not dictate through the app, because that needs your hotkey.
- Disk has 2.6 GB free and swap is 2,640 of 3,072 MB used. Freeing space is up to you; I deleted nothing of yours.
- Nothing is committed.

### Next steps
- I will report the second check's result by 12:33 and fix any failure it finds.
- Dictate once now and once after a break, then compare how long the text takes to appear.
- Free some disk space to reduce swap use.

In my tests after memory pressure, a 5 s dictation now finishes 0.9 to 1.1 s after release with a 3 s hold, against 5.8 to 6.2 s without these changes.
